app_purpose: Java XML/object serialization library used by web services/apps to reconstruct objects from untrusted XML (or JSON); apps that expose an endpoint calling new XStream().fromXML(untrusted) out of the box deserialize the concrete type named in the stream, relying on XStream's default security deny-list to refuse dangerous types. Here it is fronted by a REAL Java HTTP service (com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) whose POST /deser deserializes the XML request body via new XStream().fromXML().
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502): new XStream().fromXML() resolves and processes the type named in the stream, and a dangerous trigger type reaches an RCE sink (java.lang.ProcessBuilder). The guard is XStream's DEFAULT deny-list (XStream.setupSecurity(), applied by the constructor); it is an enumerated blacklist (default-allow via AnyTypePermission.ANY minus specific denyTypes/denyTypesByRegExp), so any dangerous trigger type name not in the set still deserializes (CWE-184, incomplete list of disallowed inputs)

flag.resource: XStream's DEFAULT deny-list (XStream.setupSecurity() / TypePermission blacklist, applied by `new XStream()`) that the CVE-2013-7285 hardening grew to keep dangerous trigger types (java.beans.EventHandler, later java.lang.ProcessBuilder) from being deserialized; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir that the HTTP service echoes only when fromXML() gets PAST that deny check for the named trigger type
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at container start. An EXTERNAL HTTP POST /deser carries the XML body <list><TRIGGER/><pcb.PcbCanary/></list>, which the service deserializes with the REAL new XStream().fromXML(); XStream deny-checks TRIGGER first and, only if PERMITTED, reaches the benign shadow bean <pcb.PcbCanary/>, whose registered converter reads that file, stashes the token in com.pcb.CanaryHolder, and the service echoes it in the HTTP response. Absent from XStream source, the service code and the crafted payload.
flag.detect: POST an XML body naming a trigger type to the REAL new XStream().fromXML() sink behind the HTTP service; the version's own unmodified default deny-list (setupSecurity) decides whether XStream processes the type past the guard (reaching the benign pcb.PcbCanary shadow bean) or throws ForbiddenClassException -> the flag token appears in the HTTP response iff the type was permitted

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: XStream advisory CVE-2020-26217: the RCE 'is a variation of CVE-2013-7285' (also previously reported as CVE-2017-9805 for the Struts XStream plugin); 'All versions until and including version 1.4.13 are affected, if using the version out of the box'; fixed in 1.4.14. The -26217 chain reaches java.lang.ProcessBuilder via the NEW trigger type javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter. Confirmed EMPIRICALLY on real Docker against the pinned XStream jars' own default deny-list (setupSecurity() of `new XStream()`): 1.4.10 permits java.beans.EventHandler (NO denyTypes / AnyTypePermission.ANY only); 1.4.13 DENIES java.beans.EventHandler (the CVE-2013-7285 trigger) but PERMITS javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter -> incomplete; 1.4.14 DENIES javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter == the CVE-2020-26217 fix. Runtime ForbiddenClassException observed for the denied names per version (see repro.log). CVE-2013-7285 advisory (x-stream.github.io/CVE-2013-7285.html): dynamic-proxy + java.beans.EventHandler + java.lang.ProcessBuilder.
